how_to_read: Each case has an id, the rule it covers (the numbered rules of docs/areas.md section 2; 'concurrency', 'tooling' and 'examples' name the section), a kind (decide, reuse, report, validate), an input and the exact expected output. wrong_implementation names a plausible wrong implementation that the case fails. In decide and reuse the areas file is input.areas_file, or input.legacy (the land.conf keys of a repository with no areas file: the implicit area `all` stands for it); input.land_inert and input.protected are the LAND_INERT and LAND_PROTECTED patterns, input.release_candidate says this run is the release candidate. A change is [status, path] with status A, M or D, or [R, old, new]. Every list in expect is in the order the spec defines (names sorted; steps in the order of the areas in the file, then of their steps, a step that two areas share run once). input.facts is information an implementation must ignore. docs/areas.md section 10 is the full format.

cases.about: a path owned by one area touches that area and runs ALL of its steps, in file order
cases.wrong_implementation: narrows the steps by where the change is: runs only make lint-app (cwd src/app) and drops make fmt-check and make test-app

cases.about: src/lib/* is in the paths of lib and app: the path touches BOTH, and a step two areas share (make fmt-check) runs once
cases.wrong_implementation: first match wins (touches lib only), or selects by import graph and runs only the area that imports the symbol

cases.about: * matches any run of characters, / included: site/api/v1/x.json is owned by site/* AND by site/api/*, so both are touched
cases.wrong_implementation: pathname globbing, where * stops at /: neither glob matches, and only the enclosing site-api runs

cases.about: tests/lib/* belongs to lib only. app uses the library, but there are no edges between areas: app is not touched
cases.wrong_implementation: adds a dependency edge (everything that depends on lib runs)

cases.about: tools/vendor/* is excluded from tools and owned by vendor: only vendor is touched
cases.wrong_implementation: ignores exclude, so tools is touched too

cases.about: Docs/a.md is not docs/*: no area owns or encloses it, so it is unmapped and the whole suite runs
cases.wrong_implementation: a case-insensitive matcher touches docs and runs nothing

cases.about: scripts/release.sh: no area owns it and no area encloses it: UNMAPPED. The full suite runs and the path is named
cases.wrong_implementation: skips a path no area owns

cases.about: scripts/x.sh matches no glob. root-docs owns two root files by name, and a glob that starts in the repository root encloses NOTHING (or an area at the root would swallow every unmapped path): UNMAPPED, full suite
cases.wrong_implementation: treats the root as a directory that encloses every path: root-docs absorbs it and the alarm never rings

cases.about: core/io/data.json matches no glob. core (directory core) and core-io (directory core/io) both enclose it: the LONGEST directory wins, core-io alone
cases.wrong_implementation: takes the first enclosing area (core), or all enclosing areas

cases.about: core/iodata.json: the enclosing directory is a PATH prefix, not a string prefix. core/io does not enclose core/iodata.json; core does
cases.wrong_implementation: compares by string prefix (core/io is a prefix of core/iodata.json), so core-io wins

cases.about: x/y/z.bin matches no glob. notes-md and notes-txt start in the same directory x/y: areas that tie ALL run
cases.wrong_implementation: first-tied-wins

cases.about: core/gen/a.py is excluded from core, so core does not enclose it either: unmapped, full suite
cases.wrong_implementation: applies exclude to ownership but not to the closest-enclosing rule (it runs core alone)

cases.about: other/f.txt: no area encloses it: unmapped, full suite
cases.wrong_implementation: skips it

cases.about: a DELETED path matches areas like any other path
cases.wrong_implementation: ignores deletions (nothing is touched)

cases.about: a rename is a deletion of the old path plus an addition of the new one; both ends are matched
cases.wrong_implementation: matches the new path only (app alone) or the old path only (lib alone)

cases.about: a rename whose old end is owned and whose new end is not: the unmapped end alone makes the suite full
cases.wrong_implementation: looks at the old path only

cases.about: docs has no steps: the change touches it, runs nothing, and the verdict says inert (the area list says why), never a bare green
cases.wrong_implementation: treats a stepless area as unmapped and runs everything

cases.about: a change to a stepless area and to a real one runs the real one's steps; it is not inert
cases.wrong_implementation: lets one stepless path make the whole change inert

cases.about: a change under .land/ (the areas file is .land/areas.json) judges the judge: it runs every area and is named gate-defining, not unmapped
cases.wrong_implementation: finds no owner, no enclosing area and runs nothing, or runs the full suite but names the path unmapped

cases.about: a path in LAND_PROTECTED runs every area even when an area owns it, and is named gate-defining
cases.wrong_implementation: ignores LAND_PROTECTED (touches tools only)

cases.about: the release candidate runs EVERY area whatever the change: a docs-only change run as a candidate runs all steps
cases.wrong_implementation: applies the narrowing to the candidate

cases.about: LAND_INERT keeps working beside an areas file: it is the pseudo-area inert, which owns its patterns (not deleted paths) and has no steps
cases.wrong_implementation: drops LAND_INERT when an areas file exists (CHANGELOG.md is then unmapped and runs everything)

cases.about: an inert path beside a path of a real area: the real area's steps run, inert is listed as touched
cases.wrong_implementation: skips everything when any path is inert

cases.about: a DELETED inert path is not owned by inert (a check can read that a file exists): no area owns it, so it is unmapped and the suite is full
cases.wrong_implementation: lets a deleted path be inert

cases.about: a path in three areas touches all three
cases.wrong_implementation: stops at the first owner

cases.about: a repository with only LAND_TEST_CMD is one implicit area `all` that owns everything
cases.wrong_implementation: requires an areas file, or leaves a path of the root unmapped

cases.about: LAND_GATES_CMD runs before LAND_TEST_CMD; both are steps of the implicit area
cases.wrong_implementation: runs the test command first or drops the gates command

cases.about: LAND_INERT: every changed path inert, nothing runs, the verdict is inert
cases.wrong_implementation: implicit area does not yield to inert, so it also runs make test

cases.about: LAND_INERT: one path that is not inert and the whole of Tier 1 runs
cases.wrong_implementation: skips on any inert path

cases.about: LAND_INERT: a deleted inert path runs Tier 1
cases.wrong_implementation: treats a deletion as inert

cases.about: LAND_INERT: a code file renamed INTO an inert path is seen leaving its old path, and Tier 1 runs
cases.wrong_implementation: looks only at the new path of a rename

cases.about: LAND_PROTECTED: a protected path is never inert; the whole of Tier 1 runs
cases.wrong_implementation: lets the inert pattern win over protected

cases.about: the trunk moved in docs only; my change touches app: the move touches no area of mine, so my verdict stands
cases.wrong_implementation: re-validates on any trunk move

cases.about: the trunk moved in tests/app of another area; my change is in lib's own tests: disjoint areas, reuse
cases.wrong_implementation: re-validates on any trunk move

cases.about: the trunk moved src/app/b.c; I changed src/app/a.c: a DIFFERENT FILE of the same area still re-validates the area (file-level reuse is unsound here: the area's steps read both)
cases.wrong_implementation: file-level reuse (the same file only): it reuses a verdict that b.c may have invalidated

cases.about: I changed src/app/a.c (app); the trunk moved src/lib/x.c, a path of lib AND app: the move touches app too (overlap is the declared dependency), so app re-validates even though the two paths differ
cases.wrong_implementation: attributes a moved path to its first owner only (lib), so the move seems to touch no area of mine and app's verdict is wrongly reused

cases.about: I changed tests/lib/t.c (lib); the trunk moved src/lib/x.c, a path of lib AND app: lib re-validates
cases.wrong_implementation: reuses because the moved path is not literally one of mine

cases.about: the trunk moved a path no area owns: it runs the full suite, so every area of mine re-validates
cases.wrong_implementation: treats an unmapped moved path as touching nothing

cases.about: the trunk moved the areas file: what judges a change moved, so every area of mine re-validates
cases.wrong_implementation: reuses across a change of the areas file

cases.about: my change touches the areas file: it runs every area, so nothing is reused even when the move is in docs
cases.wrong_implementation: reuses the verdict of a change that edits the judge

cases.about: my change touches docs only (no steps): nothing ran, so there is nothing to re-run or to reuse; both lists are empty
cases.wrong_implementation: lists the stepless area as re-run or reused (an area with no steps ran nothing)

cases.about: the trunk renamed a file from src/lib to tools: both ends count; lib and app are touched by the move
cases.wrong_implementation: matches only the new end of a moved rename, which is in tools

cases.about: land-check: every pair of overlapping areas with the paths in the overlap, every tracked path no area owns (with the areas that would enclose it: empty when it is unmapped), and the areas with no steps. .land/ is the lander's own and is not listed
cases.wrong_implementation: omits the overlap or the unowned list

cases.about: a tracked path no glob matches but an area encloses is reported unowned with the enclosing areas; one nobody encloses is reported with an empty list
cases.wrong_implementation: reports only the paths no area encloses (it hides the paths that merely fall back to an enclosing area)

cases.about: with LAND_INERT, the pseudo-area inert is reported like any area: its patterns, its overlap and its no-steps entry
cases.wrong_implementation: ignores LAND_INERT in the report

cases.about: a well-formed areas file
cases.wrong_implementation: rejects it

cases.about: two areas with the same name
cases.wrong_implementation: does not enforce this rule and accepts the file

cases.about: the name inert is reserved for LAND_INERT
cases.wrong_implementation: does not enforce this rule and accepts the file

cases.about: a name is [a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*
cases.wrong_implementation: does not enforce this rule and accepts the file

cases.about: an unknown key is an error, as in land.conf (a typo must not switch a gate off)
cases.wrong_implementation: does not enforce this rule and accepts the file

cases.about: an area must own something
cases.wrong_implementation: does not enforce this rule and accepts the file

cases.about: paths are relative to the repository root
cases.wrong_implementation: does not enforce this rule and accepts the file

cases.about: a path may not climb out
cases.wrong_implementation: does not enforce this rule and accepts the file

cases.about: a step is {run, cwd?}
cases.wrong_implementation: does not enforce this rule and accepts the file

cases.about: a working directory is a literal directory
cases.wrong_implementation: does not enforce this rule and accepts the file

cases.about: steps is required; an area with no steps says so with []
cases.wrong_implementation: does not enforce this rule and accepts the file

cases.about: version is exactly 1
cases.wrong_implementation: does not enforce this rule and accepts the file

cases.about: the glob language is * and ? only
cases.wrong_implementation: does not enforce this rule and accepts the file

cases.about: src/app/main.c is changed. By the facts, the steps of lib read src/app/main.c (an escape that the release candidate will find): the contract still touches app ONLY. There is no selection by what a test read, by an import graph or by coverage

facts.note: informational: an implementation must ignore it

cases.wrong_implementation: selects by import graph, by what a test read or by coverage, and adds lib

cases.about: the same change when the facts say that only make lint-app reads the changed file: every step of the touched area still runs; nothing narrower

facts.note: informational: an implementation must ignore it

cases.wrong_implementation: selects steps or tests by coverage (it runs make lint-app only)

cases.about: a change of 12 paths in one area runs exactly the steps of that area; a large change is never turned into the full suite or into a narrower one
cases.wrong_implementation: caps by size: more than 10 paths run the full suite

cases.about: a change to the shared library touches the library and both services (each lists it)
cases.wrong_implementation: first match wins: only lib runs

cases.about: a change inside one service touches that service only
cases.wrong_implementation: adds dependency edges: the library and billing run too

cases.about: a change in web touches web only: web lists shared, shared does not list web
cases.wrong_implementation: adds dependency edges: shared runs too

cases.about: a change in shared touches shared, web and api
cases.wrong_implementation: first match wins

cases.about: a change under test/ touches the test-suite area only
cases.wrong_implementation: adds dependency edges

cases.about: a change under src/ touches all three code areas
cases.wrong_implementation: first match wins

cases.about: a header touches the library and the tools
cases.wrong_implementation: first match wins

cases.about: docs/trust-ledger.md is excluded from docs and owned by proofs: only proofs runs
cases.wrong_implementation: ignores exclude: the stepless docs area is touched too

cases.about: a change to the specification touches spec, impl and proofs, not the console
cases.wrong_implementation: first match wins

cases.about: glossary.md is listed in guide and policies: both run
cases.wrong_implementation: first match wins

cases.about: the python example of docs/areas.md is a valid areas file
cases.wrong_implementation: rejects it

cases.about: the typescript example of docs/areas.md is a valid areas file
cases.wrong_implementation: rejects it

cases.about: the haskell example of docs/areas.md is a valid areas file
cases.wrong_implementation: rejects it

cases.about: the c example of docs/areas.md is a valid areas file
cases.wrong_implementation: rejects it

cases.about: the lean example of docs/areas.md is a valid areas file
cases.wrong_implementation: rejects it

cases.about: the documents example of docs/areas.md is a valid areas file
cases.wrong_implementation: rejects it

cases.about: Makefile is read by every step (each runs make): it is in every area's paths, so a change to it runs all three areas
cases.wrong_implementation: treats the Makefile as unmapped and names it, or lists it in the library area only
